Explain Ohm's law simply.
V = IR. Voltage equals current times resistance — if you know two, you can solve for the third.
What's the formula for torque?
T = F × r — force times the distance from the pivot point.
What's the difference between series and parallel circuits?
Series: same current, voltage splits across components. Parallel: same voltage, current splits across branches.
How do I calculate power in a circuit?
P = VI — power equals voltage times current. You can also use P = I²R or P = V²/R depending on what you know.
What's Newton's second law?
F = ma — force equals mass times acceleration.
Explain the difference between stress and strain.
Stress is force per unit area (how hard something's being pushed/pulled). Strain is the resulting deformation, a ratio of change in length to original length.
What is a moment of inertia?
It's a measure of an object's resistance to rotational acceleration — depends on mass distribution relative to the axis of rotation.
How do I size a beam for a given load?
Depends on load type, span, material, and allowable deflection/stress. Give me the specifics and I'll walk through it.
What's the difference between AC and DC current?
DC flows in one constant direction. AC periodically reverses direction, typically in a sine wave pattern.
Explain the first law of thermodynamics.
Energy can't be created or destroyed, only converted between forms — total energy in a closed system stays constant.
What's a PID controller?
A feedback control loop using Proportional, Integral, and Derivative terms to minimize error between a desired setpoint and actual output.
How do gears change torque and speed?
Smaller gear driving a larger one increases torque but reduces speed, and vice versa — the ratio is inversely proportional.
What is yield strength?
The stress at which a material starts to deform permanently instead of returning to its original shape.
Explain Bernoulli's principle.
As fluid speed increases, its pressure decreases — that's why airflow over a wing's curved top creates lift.
What's the difference between voltage and current?
Voltage is the electrical potential difference driving current. Current is the actual flow of charge.
How do capacitors work?
They store energy in an electric field between two plates, charging and discharging based on voltage changes.
What's a safety factor in engineering design?
A multiplier applied to expected loads to account for uncertainty — ensures the design can handle more than the minimum required.
Explain resonance in mechanical systems.
When a system is driven at its natural frequency, amplitude builds up rapidly — can cause failure if uncontrolled, like the Tacoma Narrows bridge.
What's the purpose of a heat sink?
It increases surface area to dissipate heat faster, keeping components like CPUs or power transistors from overheating.
How does a transformer step down voltage?
Via the turns ratio between primary and secondary coils — fewer turns on the secondary side lowers output voltage.
Debug this for loop, it's not working.
Paste the code and tell me what it should do versus what it's actually doing.
What's the difference between a list and a tuple in Python?
Lists are mutable, tuples aren't. Otherwise they behave similarly.
Explain recursion simply.
A function that calls itself, breaking a problem into smaller versions of itself until it hits a base case.
What's a race condition?
When two processes access shared data at the same time and the outcome depends on timing — leads to unpredictable bugs.
What does Big O notation measure?
How an algorithm's runtime or memory use scales as input size grows.
What's the difference between == and === in JavaScript?
== compares values with type coercion. === compares value and type, no coercion.
Explain what an API is.
A defined way for one piece of software to talk to another — a set of rules for requests and responses.
What's a null pointer exception?
You're trying to use a reference that doesn't actually point to anything — usually forgot to initialize a variable.
What is version control used for?
Tracking changes to code over time, so you can revert, branch, and collaborate without overwriting each other's work.
Explain the difference between synchronous and asynchronous code.
Synchronous runs one step at a time, blocking until each finishes. Asynchronous lets other work happen while waiting on something slow, like a network call.
What's a memory leak?
Memory that's allocated but never released, even though it's no longer needed — builds up over time and can crash a program.
How does a hash table work?
It maps keys to values using a hash function, giving near-constant time lookups.
What's the difference between compiled and interpreted languages?
Compiled languages are translated to machine code ahead of time. Interpreted languages are executed line-by-line at runtime.
Explain what Git rebase does.
It replays your commits on top of another branch's latest changes, creating a cleaner, linear history than a merge.
What's a deadlock?
Two or more processes waiting on each other to release a resource — neither can proceed.
What's the difference between speed and velocity?
Speed is how fast something moves. Velocity is speed with direction.
Explain entropy simply.
A measure of disorder in a system — it tends to increase over time in a closed system.
What's the Pythagorean theorem?
a² + b² = c² — relates the sides of a right triangle, where c is the hypotenuse.
What's the difference between mass and weight?
Mass is the amount of matter in an object, constant everywhere. Weight is the force of gravity on that mass, which changes with location.
Explain the difference between an atom and a molecule.
An atom is a single element's smallest unit. A molecule is two or more atoms bonded together.
What's a derivative in calculus?
The rate of change of a function at a given point — the slope of the tangent line.
What's the difference between a hypothesis and a theory?
A hypothesis is a testable prediction. A theory is a well-substantiated explanation supported by extensive evidence.
Explain how a battery works.
A chemical reaction moves electrons from the negative to positive terminal through an external circuit, producing current.
What is the speed of light?
About 299,792,458 meters per second in a vacuum.
What's the difference between exothermic and endothermic reactions?
Exothermic reactions release energy, usually as heat. Endothermic reactions absorb energy from their surroundings.
